I'm working on the Gleam compiler and I'd like to add a new warning for a JavaScript-specific limitation in bit array pattern matching.

*   When compiling for the JavaScript target, if a bit array pattern contains an integer segment with a compile-time literal size greater than 52 bits (expressed either as a bare integer literal or via the size() option), the compiler must emit a warning.

*   The warning title for an oversized JavaScript bit array integer segment must be exactly: 'Truncated bit array segment'.

*   The warning body for an oversized JavaScript bit array integer segment must state the exact bit size and the JavaScript limit: 'This segment is a {N}-bit long integer, but on the JavaScript target numbers have at most 52 bits. It would be truncated to its first 52 bits.' where {N} is replaced with the actual size.

*   The warning hint for an oversized JavaScript bit array integer segment must be exactly: 'Did you mean to use the `bytes` segment option?'

*   The warning must only be emitted when the size is compile-time known and strictly greater than 52. Integer segments with size 52 or below must not trigger this warning.

*   The warning must only be emitted when the pattern segment binds a variable (e.g., `<<n:size(53)>>` or `<<number:123>>`); patterns that do not capture a value in the segment do not require this warning.

*   Existing warning messages for 'todo found', 'panic used as a function', and 'todo used as a function' must not have a blank line between the main warning body text and the 'Hint:' line — the hint must immediately follow the body text.

*   The 'Inefficient use of list.length' warning body text must be formatted as a single reflowed paragraph without a trailing blank line before the hint. The body must read: 'The `list.length` function has to iterate across the whole list to calculate the length, which is wasteful if you only need to know if the list is empty or not.'


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll explore the codebase to understand the warning system structure before implementing.

# Gleam Compiler Warning System — Research Report

## Architecture Overview

There are **two** `Warning` enums:
- **`type_::error::Warning`** — emitted by the type checker/analyser (this is where your new warning almost certainly belongs).
- **`warning::Warning`** — a top-level wrapper that includes `Warning::Type { path, src, warning: type_::Warning }` and other non-type warnings. Its `to_diagnostic()` method is where all diagnostics (title/body/hint/labels) are formatted.

---

## 1 & 2. Warning definitions and diagnostic formatting

### The type-checker warning enum
`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/type_/error.rs`
- `pub enum Warning` starts at **line 854**.
- Example variants relevant to you:
  - `Todo { kind, location, type_ }` — line **855**
  - `InefficientEmptyListCheck { location, kind }` — line **931**
  - `TodoOrPanicUsedAsFunction { kind, location, arguments_location, arguments }` — line **1042**
  - `BitArraySegmentTruncatedValue { location, truncation }` — line **1102** (the closest analog to a bit-array warning)
- **`fn location(&self) -> SrcSpan`** — line **1385**. Every variant is matched here in a big `|`-chain (lines 1387–1426). **A new variant with a `location` field must be added to this match** or it won't compile.
- `TodoOrPanic` enum (used by `TodoOrPanicUsedAsFunction`) — line **1256**.
- `EmptyListCheckKind` is referenced by `InefficientEmptyListCheck`.

### Diagnostic formatting (title / text / hint / labels)
`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/warning.rs`
- `impl Warning` — line **245**; `pub fn to_diagnostic(&self) -> Diagnostic` — line **246**.
- Type warnings are matched under a `Warning::Type { path, src, warning }` arm; each `type_::Warning::*` variant produces a `Diagnostic { title, text, hint, level, location }`.
- Specific examples:
  - `type_::Warning::Todo` → title `"Todo found"` / `"Incomplete block"` / etc. — lines **427–479** (note the `match kind` for the title at line 438, and the hint appended at line 458).
  - `type_::Warning::InefficientEmptyListCheck` → title `"Inefficient use of \`list.length\`"` — lines **775–804** (shows using `hint: Some(...)`).
  - `type_::Warning::TodoOrPanicUsedAsFunction` → titles `"Todo used as a function"` / `"Panic used as a function"` — lines **1101–1156**.
  - `type_::Warning::BitArraySegmentTruncatedValue` → title `"Truncated bit array segment"` — lines **1318–1370** (best template to copy: builds a `text` string with `wrap(&text)`, sets a label with span).
- Helpers available in this file: `wrap(&text)`, `pluralise(...)`. `Diagnostic`, `Location`, `diagnostic::Label`, `diagnostic::Level::Warning` come from the `crate::diagnostic` module.

### Where warnings are emitted (pushed)
`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/type_/expression.rs` uses `self.problems.warning(Warning::...)`:
- `Warning::Todo` — line **569**
- `Warning::TodoOrPanicUsedAsFunction` — line **1196**
- `Warning::BitArraySegmentTruncatedValue` — line **1774** (inside bit-array segment inference for expressions)
- `Warning::InefficientEmptyListCheck` — line **1984**

The mechanism is `self.problems.warning(...)` where `problems` is a `Problems` accumulator.

---

## 3. Bit array pattern type-checking

### Pattern segment analysis
`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/type_/pattern.rs`
- `fn infer_pattern_bit_array(...)` — line **415** (iterates segments, marks the last segment).
- `fn infer_pattern_segment(mut segment, is_last_segment)` — line **444**. This is the core per-segment routine:
  - Infers options via `analyse::infer_bit_array_option(...)` — line **489**.
  - Calls `self.check_pattern_segment_size_expression(&options)` — line **496**.
  - Calls `bit_array::type_options_for_pattern(&options, !is_last_segment, self.environment.target)` — line **498** to get `segment_type` (and produce `Error::BitArraySegmentError` on failure at line 505).
  - **JavaScript-specific handling** — lines **515–573**: `if self.environment.target == Target::JavaScript && !self.current_function.has_javascript_external { ... }`. This loop inspects each `BitArrayOption`:
    - `BitArrayOption::Bits` → tracks `FeatureKind::JavaScriptUnalignedBitArray` (line 521).
    - `BitArrayOption::Size { value, .. } if segment_type.is_int()` → checks `Pattern::BitArraySize(BitArraySize::Int { int_value, .. })` where `int_value % 8 != 0` (line 529–539). **This is the exact place where an int segment with a non-byte-aligned size on JS is detected — a very likely spot for your new warning.**
- `fn check_pattern_segment_size_expression(&mut self, options)` — line **1468**: finds the `BitArrayOption::Size { value, .. }`, unwraps `Pattern::BitArraySize(size)`, and matches `BitArraySize::Int | Variable | BinaryOperator | Block`.

### Bit array option typing / validation
`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/bit_array.rs`
- `pub fn type_options_for_pattern<TypedValue>(input_options, must_have_size, target)` — line **23** → delegates to `type_options(...)` (line 93) with `TypeOptionsMode::Pattern`.
- `type_options(...)` (line 93) does all category validation: conflicting size/type/endianness/signedness, target-specific rejections (e.g. `Native`/utf-codepoint on JavaScript — lines 108–163), `SegmentMustHaveSize` (line 218), zero/negative constant size rejected in patterns (lines 327–334).
- `struct SegmentOptionCategories` — line **39** (holds `type_`, `signed`, `endian`, `unit`, `size`).
- `trait GetLiteralValue` / `as_int_literal()` — line **339** (how a size expression's literal int value is extracted; `TypedPattern` impl at line 343).
- `enum ErrorType` — line **391** (all bit-array error kinds, e.g. `ConflictingSizeOptions`, `SegmentMustHaveSize`, `ConstantSizeNotPositive`, `OptionNotSupportedForTarget`).

Note: the AST uses `BitArrayOption` (in `ast.rs`) with a `Size { value, .. }` variant; there is no separate `SizeOption` type — sizes are `BitArrayOption::Size`. Sizes in patterns are represented by `BitArraySize` (`Int`, `Variable`, `BinaryOperator`, `Block`) — see `ast::BitArraySize` and `TypedBitArraySize`.

---

## 4. How the target is known during pattern type-checking

`/workspace/repo/compiler-core/src/type_/environment.rs`
- `pub struct Environment` has `pub target: Target` (line **21**) and `pub target_support: TargetSupport` (line 23). `Target` comes from `crate::build::Target` (enum `Erlang | JavaScript`).
- In pattern code it is accessed as **`self.environment.target`** (e.g. pattern.rs lines 501, 515). Compared against `Target::JavaScript` / `Target::Erlang`.
- The target is set when the `Environment` is constructed (environment.rs `new(...)`, target threaded in at lines 119/138), originating from the build/compilation configuration.

Implementation complete and verified end-to-end. Here's a summary of the changes (all in source files, none in `tests/`):

## New warning: oversized JavaScript bit array integer segment

**`compiler-core/src/type_/error.rs`**
- Added the `Warning::JavaScriptIntUnalignedSegmentTooLarge { location, size }` variant, storing the size as a `BigInt`.
- Added it to the `location()` match.

**`compiler-core/src/type_/pattern.rs`** (`infer_pattern_segment`)
- Restructured the existing JavaScript-target `BitArraySize::Int` arm so it handles both the pre-existing unaligned-feature tracking (`% 8 != 0`) and the new check. When the target is JavaScript, the segment is an integer with a compile-time literal size `> 52`, **and** the segment value binds a variable (`segment.value.is_variable()`), it emits the warning.

**`compiler-core/src/warning.rs`** (`to_diagnostic`)
- Added the diagnostic: title `"Truncated bit array segment"`, body `"This segment is a {N}-bit long integer, but on the JavaScript target numbers have at most 52 bits. It would be truncated to its first 52 bits."` (reflowed via `wrap`), hint ``"Did you mean to use the `bytes` segment option?"``.

**`language-server/src/code_action.rs`**
- Added the new variant to an exhaustive `type_::Warning` match (returns `None`, matching the other non-actionable warnings).

## Existing-warning formatting fixes (`compiler-core/src/warning.rs`)
- `Todo` and `TodoOrPanicUsedAsFunction`: changed `\n\nHint:` → `\nHint:` so the hint immediately follows the body.
- `InefficientEmptyListCheck`: body is now a single `wrap`-reflowed paragraph with no trailing newline, so no blank line precedes the hint.

## Verification
Built the full workspace, then compiled a temp JS-target project:
- `<<n:size(53)>>` → warns ✓; `<<number:123>>` → warns ✓
- `<<ok:52>>` (52, not `> 52`) → no warning ✓
- `<<_:size(60)>>` (discard) and `<<5:size(70)>>` (literal) → no warning ✓ (don't bind a variable)
- Erlang target → 0 truncation warnings ✓
- Confirmed the todo / panic / `list.length` warnings now render the hint directly under the body.

The verification system will apply the test/snapshot patches automatically.
